A_claims.source_locator: Main PDF p4 Fig1C/D + p18 methods
A_claims.source_proposition: External category-A probabilities exactly set of five {0.2,0.35,0.5,0.65,0.8}; stepwise change every 80–120 trials randomly chosen excluding previous state; no explicit new-block cue
Externally sampled Gaussian category stimulus orientation and participant sensory measurement uncertainty form source task likelihood, not participant-controlled world dynamics
Covert task subject makes trial-level binary orientation category keypress after stimulus; receives explicit true-category feedback
Overt task subject reports continuous oriented decision boundary BEFORE stimulus then sees category feedback, has separate adjustment noise
Original 11 observers (one author) complete 200 familiarization training then 800 experimental trials per original covert/overt session and independent sensory measurement session

A_claims.source_locator: Main PDF p5 Eq1, official S1 pp3–8
A_claims.source_proposition: Ideal Bayes observer posterior over possible run lengths and previous category probability state with Markov transition dependence, then marginalizes to category-A predicted prior
Exact original Bayesian recursive posterior separates conditional category prediction, predecessor run-length and previous-state joint posterior; P13 source extends Adams-MacKay prior formalism
Change-point hazard on source 80–120 run length and previous-state transition; full source future-state Markov dependence cannot be replaced by memoryless independent hazard only
Original Bayesian joint posterior U(r,ξ|C1:t) and boundary initialized r=0 uniform previous state; covert likelihood/noise/lapse and overt optimal criterion distinct task output equations

Bayes_r assumes wrong run-length interval, Bayes_pi assumes wrong possible probability-state set, Bayes_beta assumes symmetric neutral-prior Beta hyperprior; original three variants alter different knowledge

A_claims.source_locator: Main PDF p6 and S1 pp10–11
A_claims.source_proposition: Flexible Bayes_rπβ varies run-length interval, state range and beta-neutral hyperprior together with FIVE extra parameters, not included routine 11-model Fig3/Table1 standard fit and separately scored BIC/ELBO
Fixed criterion source sets neutral z=(μB+μA)/2 independent of learned category probability; not zero sensory likelihood in covert version
Exp initial category probability p_hat1=0.5 and delta update p_hat_t+1=α C_t+(1-α)p_hat_t, source direct one-step category feedback each trial
Expbias first updates source Exp p_hat then linear mixes with stable neutral 0.5, weight w. Two distinct described conceptual timescales, not observed neural compartments
Source Wilson 2013 approximate three-node variable integration with hazard-dependent weights l1=1 and l2,l3,nu_p fitted; original Wilson plus later correction is predecessor comparator
Main RL comparator updates decision criterion z only if response incorrect; unlike Exp, this model need not represent a probability state
Original appendix's separate RL_prob updates probability only after incorrect feedback, explicitly NOT source main Eq7 criterion-only RL; its fit no unique superiority

Original Behrens et al 2007 Bayesian comparator tracks probability pi, volatility v and volatility-change k via approximate five-dimensional grid and marginalization; unrelated to P13 new theorem provenance

A_claims.source_locator: Main PDF p5/S1 p7 task model
A_claims.source_proposition: Bayesian and probability-estimator models convert predicted category prior into decision criterion or covert posterior odds with separate visual-noise and adjustment-noise channels
Both task observations show criterion or category response change following external prior shifts, no fixed criterion best fit; overt reports fluctuate between true changes
Multiple source computational model output shapes capture visible trends; figure shaded source 68% model-response intervals, not proof model semantic identity with brain
Original main 11-comparator model selection favors Expbias among that comparator set, source group protected exceedance φ=0.96 covert, 0.86 overt

A_claims.source_locator: Main PDF pp11–12 Fig3 and S1 FigS1
A_claims.source_proposition: Flexible five-additional-param Bayes_rπβ vs Expbias BIC and ELBO separately compared, neither task distinguishes statistically; do not report Bayesian ruled out
Original group best model 6 of 11 in each task; source cross-task standardized LML score correlation r0.60, but individual best models can differ

A_claims.source_locator: Main PDF p14 Fig5 / Tables1–2 p15
A_claims.source_proposition: Overt Expbias alpha0.22±0.03 w0.74±0.06 vs covert alpha0.17±0.04 w0.58±0.05; original w task difference significant and alpha not

A_claims.source_locator: Main PDF p13–14 and p15 Discussion
A_claims.source_proposition: Source average fitted category-history time constant approx4.5 trials vs true hazard expected run100, reflects fast perceived changes during longer real blocks, not environmental truth
Simple Expbias considered more biologically plausible by authors but cannot distinguish flexible Bayes, actual algorithm/hierarchical state latent not measured by behavior alone
Source model recovery on 1980 simulated datasets per generative model/task, ~70% across tasks with RL mistaken for Exp in covert; not 100% identifiability
Original overt criterion adjustment-noise σ_a fitted upward bias in parameter recovery, source authors argue LML model comparisons not affected; distinguish estimates vs fit-score confidence
Original trial-specific category feedback externally reveals true C_t every trial; posterior over observed labels not latent unsupervised state inference about never-reported categories
Separate main covert and overt likelihood and lapse/noise differ; individual trial 800 per task after 200 training, cannot pool task-specific observation interfaces into identical response density
Original report model scoring favors source-specific neutral bias, not universal adaptive lifelong learning or direct neural demonstration that stable prior is literal physical storage
Original author published model/data code exists at lacerbi/ChangeProb; current G1 does not run original inference code or independently reproduce numeric curves

A_claims.source_locator: S1 original p10 variants and p11
A_claims.source_proposition: Source S1 Bayes_bias and Bayes_rβ extra competitors and RL_prob were also considered in appendix, not just nine main-text Eqs alone; source outcome constrains exclusions
